pr_title: Propagate the keying state in the inspector
pr_body:
Toggling the keying state does not significantly change the structure of the inspector. So it's ok to propagate the keying state and then use `queue_redraw()` to update the keying icon.

Fixes #70588.
Supersedes #70616.

issue_context.title: I can't move to Animation player when I open a AnimatedSprite
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot 4-beta10

### System information

Linux, KDE Neon, OpenGL3, Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics (CML GT2)

### Issue description

I can't move to Animation player when I open a AnimatedSprite

See the video:
https://youtu.be/_nyN42rNlTw


### Steps to reproduce

- Open Scene GPlayer
- Select Idle (Animation player) node
- Select Body (Animation sprite) node
- Select animation in bottom tab

### Minimal reproduction project

You can test in my game is open source and don't have many files 👍🏻 

[the-zero-day.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10304677/the-zero-day.zip)
comments:
Seems to be caused by the SpriteFrame inspector continuing to select resource and take precedence SpriteFrame editor. Maybe can't you move it to any tab other than AnimationPlayer?

By the way, your MRP is corrupted and cannot be opened in latest master. I also tried the same steps, but could not reproduce it.
Now I change the MRP, is not corruped only I am using git lfs. But I upload again 👍🏻
Thanks! I could reproduce this. It is possibly that AnimationPlayer's update to display the keying button is conflicting with something, but without looking into it, I can't be sure.

Investigated. The cause is the sub-inspector and focusing process changing between Beta8 and Beta9. When you click on the Animation tab, the keying buttons appear in the properties, but this update causes the sub-inspector to re-activate and the SpriteFrameEditor becomes active again.
This seems to affect all editor plugins that have a bottom panel editor. They always try to show the bottom panel editor when the associated editor property is focused.

review_comments:
After all, this is just like SpecialCase in #70616, and for every additional implementation like `keying` in the EditorInspector, we need to add a line similar to this one. But it would work better than #70616.

It is preferred to add a comment as to why this line is needed in case someone later adds an implementation to the EditorInspector.

At this time, the property tree of the sub inspector has not been fully established (`_update_tree()` will be called at the end of the frame), and `EditorInspector::set_keying()` is not registered in `ClassDB`, so `Node::propagate_call()` has no effect on it. The code here is not needed if the method is registered.

Here is judged by this condition: the opened editor is an editor for editing sub-resources, so it will not be the Animation editor.

I think you can do
```suggestion
	main_vbox->propagate_call(SNAME("set_keying"), { keying }, true);
```
It doesn't seem to work, and an error is reported when compiling: `error: no matching constructor for initialization of 'const Array &'`.
Ah right, it's only possible with Vector.
